description_preview:
Description
Do you thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment?
Do you have a passion for AI systems and computing platforms that enable them?
Are you a continuous learner who enjoys solving complex technical problems and working collaboratively with researchers, developers, and infrastructure teams? If so, we're looking for someone like you to join our team at APL.
The AI Solutions Engineer combines AI platform engineering with hands-on researcher enablement. You will serve as a technical bridge between researchers and the organization's scalable AI computing platform. You will also work directly with researchers to move AI workloads from experimentation to large-scale GPU execution, providing expertise across Jupyter, containers, Kubernetes, GPU scheduling, distributed training, and AI frameworks.
As an AI Solutions Engineer, you will …
Own the technical configuration and evolution of the AI platform by evaluating new capabilities, determining appropriate adoption, and establishing application-level configurations, standards, and best practices.
Partner with Linux and Kubernetes administrators on platform deployments, upgrades, infrastructure integration, and troubleshooting issues that span the AI platform and underlying computing environment.
Provide hands-on technical assistance to researchers and data scientists using GPU-accelerated AI/ML platforms for model development, training, fine-tuning, and inference.
Troubleshoot AI workloads across the stack, including Python environments, Jupyter, containers, Kubernetes, GPU scheduling and allocation, storage, networking, and AI frameworks.
Help researchers optimize GPU utilization and scale workloads from interactive or single-GPU experimentation to multi-GPU and multi-node distributed execution.
Develop and maintain reusable environments, workflows, automation, documentation, and operational guidance that improve platform reliability, usability, and researcher productivity.
Qualifications
You’ll meet our minimum qualifications if you…
Hold a Bachelor of Science degree or equivalent years of related professional work experience.
Have at least three (3) year experience using container-based orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes) and run-time environments (e.g. Docker).
Have hands-on experience with Jupyter environments and GPU-accelerated AI frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face, or similar technologies.
Have working knowledge of Kubernetes and GPU computing concepts sufficient to configure, integrate, and troubleshoot AI applications running in shared computing environments.
Have experience supporting researchers or developers with model training, fine-tuning, inference, workload optimization, and troubleshooting.
Have proficiency with Python and shell scripting for automation, troubleshooting, and platform integration.
Have working knowledge of machine learning concepts and model development workflows.
Can demonstrate strong problem-solving, communication, collaboration, prioritization, and continuous-learning skills.
Are able to work effectively with leadership to prioritize competing tasks.
Are able to obtain Interim Secret level security clearance by your start date and can ultimately obtain Secret level clearance. If selected, you will be subject to a government security clearance investigation and must meet the requirements for access to classified information. Eligibility requirements include U.S. citizenship.
Desired Qualifications
Experience with AI workload orchestration and GPU scheduling platforms such as Run:ai, Slurm, Kubernetes-based GPU scheduling, or equivalent technologies.
Experience with NVIDIA GPU platforms and technologies such as CUDA, NVIDIA GPU Operator, NCCL, or NVIDIA Container Toolkit.
Experience supporting distributed AI training across multiple GPUs and/or multiple compute nodes.
Experience building and supporting containerized Jupyter environments and creating reusable AI/ML development environments.
Experience with AI/ML experiment tracking and lifecycle platforms such as MLflow, Weights & Biases, Kubeflow, or similar technologies.
Understanding of high-performance storage and networking considerations for GPU-intensive AI workloads.
Familiarity with a cloud computing platform (AWS, Azure or GCP).
Special Working Conditions
Occasional weekend and other after-hours work may be required to handle and/or complete critical work to meet APL's business needs.

Why Work at APL?
The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) brings world-class expertise to our nation’s most critical defense, security, space and science challenges. While we are dedicated to solving complex challenges and pioneering new technologies, what makes us truly outstanding is our culture. We offer a vibrant, welcoming atmosphere where you can bring your authentic self to work, continue to grow, and build strong connections with inspiring teammates.
At APL, we celebrate our differences of perspectives and encourage creativity and bold, new ideas. Our employees enjoy generous benefits, including a robust education assistance program, unparalleled retirement contributions, and a healthy work/life balance. APL’s campus is located in the Baltimore-Washington metro area. Learn more about our career opportunities at https://www.jhuapl.edu/careers.

description_preview:
Introduction
At IBM, work is more than a job. It is a calling: To build. To design. To code. To consult. To think along with clients and sell. To make markets. To invent. To collaborate. Not just to do something better, but to attempt things you have never thought possible. Are you ready to lead in this new era of technology and solve some of the world's most challenging problems? If so, let's talk.
About Business Unit
IBM Cloud is the global public cloud platform from IBM, one of the most secure, scalable, and enterprise-ready cloud platforms in the world. IBM Cloud powers thousands of enterprises with Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS) offerings delivered across public, private, and hybrid cloud models.
Within IBM Cloud, the Network Underlay organization is responsible for designing, building, and operating the physical and software-defined network infrastructure that underpins IBM Cloud's global fleet of data centers. NetTools is the automation and tooling engineering team within Network Underlay. We build the software systems that allow network engineers to provision, configure, monitor, and manage network infrastructure at scale, across dozens of data centers globally.
The Network Automation mission within NetTools develops and operates three interconnected platforms: NCS/Axon (Network Configuration Service), the system that automates the full lifecycle of network switch configuration from initial rack bring-up to day-to-day operations; SSOT (Source of Truth) and Hivemind, the authoritative data stores for network configuration state in classic and next-generation data center environments respectively; and the associated monitoring, validation, and reporting pipelines that keep our network infrastructure compliant, observable, and reliable.
Your Role And Responsibilities
As a Back-End Software Engineering Intern on the NetTools Network Automation team, you will work alongside the engineers actively building and evolving the Axon/NCS platform and the SSOT/Hivemind systems. This is a hands-on engineering role: you will contribute directly to production-grade back-end services and automation pipelines that are critical to the daily operation of IBM Cloud's network infrastructure.
Your Work Will Include
Contribute to the Axon/NCS project: participate in the development of back-end Python microservices that implement Day-0 (initial network provisioning, Zero Touch Provisioning) and Day-2 (operational changes, firmware updates, configuration drift remediation) automation workflows. This includes working on REST API endpoints, YAML-driven input processing, and Jinja2-based configuration generation pipelines that produce switch conf+B30igurations deployed across IBM Cloud data centers.
Build and improve automated test coverage: help design and implement unit and integration tests for the Axon/NCS platform. One of the team's active priorities is establishing a regression test framework and test environment; the intern will make direct contributions to closing that gap, including authoring test cases, identifying edge conditions, and validating end-to-end workflow correctness.
Support SSOT and Hivemind integration work: assist in developing or improving the interfaces between NCS/Axon and the SSOT/Hivemind data platforms (backed by NetBox and CockroachDB), ensuring that network context data (rack topology, port mappings, cable connections, device inventory) is reliably consumed and validated by the automation workflows.
Reduce technical debt and improve documentation: contribute to the ongoing NCS Overhaul initiative by helping refactor tightly coupled components, improving Docker container configuration practices, and writing operational runbooks and onboarding documentation that are currently incomplete or missing.
Participate in agile delivery: work within the team's sprint-based development model: track work in Jira, attend standups and sprint ceremonies, contribute to code reviews, and share progress with cross-functional stakeholders across NetTools, Network Engineering, and Data Center Operations.
Preferred Education
Bachelor's Degree
Required Technical And Professional Expertise
Back-end development in Python: hands-on experience writing Python services or scripts, including working with data structures, JSON/YAML processing, and REST API design and consumption (e.g., Flask, FastAPI, or equivalent).
Version control with Git: ability to work collaboratively in a Git-based workflow, including branching, pull requests, and participation in code reviews.
Containerization fundamentals: familiarity with Docker, including building images, running containers, and understanding container-based service deployment. NCS runs as containerized workloads and container hygiene is an active operational concern on the team.
Understanding of REST APIs and HTTP: ability to design, implement, and consume RESTful APIs. The Axon architecture exposes Day-0 and Day-2 network build APIs consumed by multiple service teams across IBM Cloud.
Automated testing aptitude: experience writing unit or integration tests, or demonstrated understanding of why automated test coverage matters in production-critical infrastructure automation systems.
Preferred Technical And Professional Experience
Working knowledge with one or more scripting or infrastructure tools: Bash, Ansible, Python automation scripts, or equivalent configuration management tooling.
Familiarity with template engines such as Jinja2, Helm, or similar. Configuration generation in NCS is built on Jinja2 templates rendered from YAML-based rack context inputs.
Exposure to container orchestration or cloud-native platforms: Kubernetes, OpenShift, or Docker Compose. NCS services run on IBM's Fabric Container Platform (FCP/OCP).

description_preview:
Responsibilities
About the Team
The Security Engineering Watermark team is dedicated to building industry-leading watermark algorithms, services, and technologies, and to supporting cross-functional teams in protecting our users, products, and infrastructure. In today's AI-driven content generation landscape, watermarking has become a critical technology for addressing challenges such as insider risk, content provenance and authenticity, copyright protection, and large‑language model(LLM) safeguarding. In this team, you'll have a unique opportunity to gain first-hand exposure to the company's strategy on key security initiatives — particularly in building invisible watermark algorithms for AI‑generated content(AIGC) and LLM models. You will also have the chance to experience the full lifecycle of security products and services, and are encouraged to participate in solving real-world problems across TikTok/ByteDance products at scale.
As a project intern, you will have the opportunity to engage in impactful short-term projects that provide you with a glimpse of professional real-world experience. You will gain practical skills through on-the-job learning in a fast-paced work environment and develop a deeper understanding of your career interests.
Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis - we encourage you to apply early.
Successful candidates must be able to commit to at least 3 months long internship period.
Responsibilities:
Work with the team to design and develop new invisible watermark algorithms that effectively balance high robustness, high visual quality, and tamper resistance.
Explore security solutions in the AIGC era, building industry‑leading capabilities for protecting LLM copyrights and tracing the provenance of AIGC.
Partner with mentors on rapid exploration sprints: frame hypotheses, design experiments, run evaluations, and iterate quickly from concept to proof-of-concept to early productization on frontier challenges.
Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams — including product, platform, and research — to understand real-world requirements and translate them into actionable solutions.
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications
Undergraduate, or Postgraduate who is currently pursuing a degree/master in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Security, AI or other STEM disciplines.
Proven experience of grasp of computer science fundamentals (algorithms, data structures, operating systems, networking).
Proficiency in one or more backend programming languages such as Python, Go, C++, Java or similar, with familiarity with common development frameworks and a solid grasp of fundamental data structures and algorithms.
Proven skills with one or more of the following: OpenCV-based image processing, signal processing, or deep learning techniques relevant to invisible watermarking.
Preferred Qualifications
Proven experience in invisible watermark development for images, video, or audio.
Proven experience with AIGC watermarking or LLM model watermarking is a strong plus.
Proactive, optimistic mindset with a strong sense of responsibility and excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
Proven skills in communication and a collaborative team spirit.

Who we are

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Payments and Risk

Optimized Checkout and Link teams work to create best-in-class checkout experiences that enhance customer satisfaction and drive merchant conversion rates. Design, build, and maintain APIs, services, and large-scale systems that reliably and efficiently handle billions of money movement requests

title: Digital Engineer (HPC Engineer 2)
reason: Stack +62; Title fit +6; Entry +15; US +10
description_preview:
What You Will Do
This position is open for external candidates only to apply.
The High Performance Computing (HPC) Division at Los Alamos National Laboratory provides scientific computing resources consisting of some of the largest HPC systems in the world, as well as numerous large commodity cluster systems. Our Support Services Team within the HPC Systems Group (HPC-SYS) provides resources for both our internal HPC admin teams and our external users by building and maintaining RHEL systems, managing our admin- and user-facing OpenShift cluster, and supporting around 1,000 users with services such as GitLab.
We are expanding this team's charter to include the modernization of our backend infrastructure to support AI-driven and agentic workflows. The Support Services Team is seeking a Digital Engineer who can operate across two closely related domains: traditional Linux/container systems administration, and the design of secure, agent-ready data access architecture across our databases and datastores.
This is a hybrid role - roughly half of the position will continue our current systems administration mission (RHEL, OpenShift, GitLab, Ansible), and half will be dedicated to redesigning and hardening our backend so that databases, storage systems, and internal tools can be safely and reliably accessed by AI agents and automated tooling.
Core Responsibilities
Systems Administration (≈50%)
Deploy, maintain, and improve RHEL and container-based systems supporting the HPC Division
Administer and grow our OpenShift cluster, including build, test, and troubleshooting of new hardware and workflows
Support GitLab and other internal services for approximately 1,000 users
Participate in periodic on-call rotation for RHEL servers and OpenShift systems
Develop and maintain configuration management via Ansible
Mentor students, junior staff, and peers; produce technical documentation, presentations, and reports
AI-Ready Backend & Agentic Infrastructure (≈50%)
Assess and redesign backend infrastructure - databases, object storage, and other datastores - to support secure, structured access by AI agents and automated systems
Design and implement role-based access control (RBAC) across multiple heterogeneous databases and storage systems, exposed via APIs or Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces
Build, deploy, and manage MCP servers that expose internal data and tools to agentic AI systems in a controlled, auditable manner
Establish patterns and guardrails for how agentic tools discover, query, and act upon internal data, ensuring least-privilege access and traceability
Evaluate and integrate API gateways, service meshes, or proxy layers as needed to mediate agent-to-datastore communication
Collaborate with data owners, security, and application teams to define access policies, authentication/authorization models, and data governance appropriate for AI/agent consumption
Stay current on the evolving agentic AI tooling landscape (e.g., MCP, function-calling frameworks, agent orchestration platforms) and translate that knowledge into practical backend design decisions
This position will be filled at the HPC Engineer 2 level.
What You Need
Minimum Job Requirements:
Demonstrated experience building, configuring, and administering production Linux systems, including strong command-line skills and working knowledge of hardware/software security practices
Strong scripting/automation skills in Bash, Python, Perl, or similar
Experience with a centralized configuration management system such as Ansible
Experience using Git for version control
Strong understanding of containers and one or more orchestration systems such as Kubernetes or OpenShift
Practical experience with relational and/or non-relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, or similar), including access control and permissions models
Experience designing or implementing role-based access control (RBAC) for data systems, whether via native database roles, API gateways, or identity/authorization frameworks
Familiarity with API design principles (REST, GraphQL, or gRPC) and secure API authentication (OAuth2, API keys, mTLS, etc.)
Some hands-on exposure to MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, agentic frameworks, or AI tool-calling architectures - or strong, demonstrable ability to quickly ramp up in this space
Experience diagnosing system and application-level issues using tools such as perf, strace, tcpdump, vmstat
Education/Experience:
Position Requires a bachelor's in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, and 3 years of relevant experience in high performance computing or scalable AI computing, or data center environments or equivalent combination of education and experience in related field.
Desired Qualifications:
Direct experience building or operating MCP servers, or integrating datastores with agentic AI systems
Understanding of how autonomous/agentic AI tools reason about, select, and invoke external tools and data sources
Experience running virtual machines and administering OpenShift clusters
Knowledge of cloud technologies and cloud-native identity/access management
Experience integrating operational metrics into monitoring systems such as Splunk
Familiarity with data governance, audit logging, and compliance considerations relevant to AI/automated data access
Demonstrated effective communication skills and ability to work productively across technical and non-technical teams
High attention to detail, strong organizational and problem-solving skills, and the ability to independently multi-task in a fast-paced environment
An active DOE Q Clearance
Work Location:
This position will be located in Los Alamos, NM, with the potential for a hybrid work arrangement (60% onsite/40% offsite) from a location within 2 hours ground commute of this location. Reporting onsite will be required. Hybrid is at the discretion of management and can change at any time with appropriate notice.

description_preview:
Description
Every token a large language model generates depends on data reaching the right accelerator at the right moment. As AI models outgrow any single chip, the network between accelerators becomes the bottleneck that decides how fast — and how affordably — the world's largest models can serve real users. That network layer is what our team builds.
We're looking for an engineer to work at the frontier of disaggregated inference: splitting LLM serving into separate prefill and decode pools and moving the model's KV cache between them at the limit of what the hardware allows. Get it right and users get answers in milliseconds; get it wrong and the fastest accelerators in the world sit idle waiting on data. You'll build components of the high-speed transfer path that make that difference, and you'll learn to measure success in how close we run to the theoretical peak of the machine.
In This Role You Will
Build and optimize the low-level data-movement software that transfers KV cache and activations across accelerators, servers, and heterogeneous memory — over AWS's highest-performance network fabric.
Profile real workloads, find the true bottleneck, and close the gap between "it works" and "it runs fast" — pushing components toward the hardware's limit.
Work across the stack — from network transport up to the inference frameworks — learning from the teams building the chips, runtime, and models.
Deliver features that ship to our largest clusters, for our largest customers, serving the largest AI models in production.
What We're Looking For
Strong C/C++ and a genuine interest in low-level, performance-critical systems — solid command of Linux, memory, and writing fast code.
The instinct to ask "how fast could this go?" and the discipline to measure it.
Exposure to high-speed networking, HPC interconnects, or GPU/accelerator systems (RDMA, InfiniBand, libfabric, UCX, NCCL, MPI) is a strong plus; embedded-systems experience is welcome.
Prior AI/ML experience is not required — if you're a strong systems engineer eager to learn, we'll teach you the ML side.
If you like solving genuinely hard problems, working alongside HPC and ML customers, iterating fast, and shipping at a scale few places can offer, come join us. You'll work alongside senior engineers and Principal Engineers who've built this layer from the ground up, with real room to grow your scope and technical depth — on a team at the leading edge of AI/ML infrastructure.
About the team: You'd be joining Annapurna Labs, an integral part of AWS. Annapurna designs the hardware and software building blocks behind EC2 — every EC2 instance runs on hardware we designed. We specialize in the chips, systems, and software that optimize the AWS customer experience, and this team sits where AI meets the silicon and the network underneath it.
A day in the life
Annapurna Labs, a crucial part of AWS, is responsible for developing hardware and software components for EC2 infrastructure. Our team focuses on building networking solutions that for Machine Learning (ML) and High-Performance Computing (HPC) workloads on AWS.
We have mixed discipline orgs, you’d be working side by side with infrastructure experts, hardware engineers, RTL engineers, scientists & architects. Our workforce spans the globe and is truly international, you’ll find yourself working side by side with individuals from numerous countries. We take mentorship seriously, you can both expect senior mentorship and will be expected to mentor new and junior engineers.
The pace is fast as we work on the latest advancements of AI/ML, but we take the time to bond as a team and enjoy the successes. We offer flexibility in working hours, and respect WLB as a core org tenet. The team enjoys working with numerous principal-level engineers and closely with directors, career growth opportunities are certainly available. This is a role where you will always be encouraged to keep learning, the AI/ML field is fast moving and constantly evolving.
About The Team
Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship. Our senior members enjoy one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects that help our team members develop your engineering expertise so you feel empowered to take on more complex tasks in the future.
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
About AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other care

reason: Stack +28; Title fit +6; Entry +15; Exp fit +10; US +10
description_preview:
Team:
Chip Architecture
Level:
1-3 years of experience preferred — but we're very open to hiring straight out of school for the right candidate.
Location:
San Jose, CA, USA
About the Role
Broadcom's Thor Ultra NIC product line builds the datapath silicon behind next-generation SmartNICs, including the congestion-control and load-balancing logic that keeps large-scale networks fast and fair under real traffic.
This is a dual role. Day to day, you'll write Network Programming Language (NPL) — our domain-specific datapath programming language, purpose-built for implementing very high-speed packet processing behavior directly on our pipeline — implementing new and existing features on the Thor Ultra datapath. But you'll also work as a junior architect alongside our senior architects: building the behavioral models, doing the analysis, and providing the hardware-feasibility feedback that shapes how features get specified in the first place. It's a strong path for someone who wants to grow into a datapath architect while staying hands-on with real implementation.
What makes the role distinct is that it lives at the intersection of two disciplines. You can't write good NPL without understanding both the networking behavior you're implementing and the silicon architecture and microarchitecture it has to run on. We're looking for someone who is genuinely interested in operating across both — not a pure networking engineer and not a pure hardware engineer, but someone who wants to be both.
What You Will Do
Write and maintain NPL implementing datapath features on the Thor Ultra NIC product line, working from architecture specifications — including support for multiple congestion-control protocols running side by side on the same datapath.
Build behavioral/reference models (typically in Python or C/C++) as architecture-level work under senior-architect guidance: prototyping and analyzing new schemes before they're committed to a spec, giving RTL designers clear guidance on intended behavior, helping the design verification (DV) team build checkers, and unit-testing a new block's architecture before it's exercised in larger, full-chip simulations.
Feed hardware-feasibility findings back up to protocol and system architects — what turns out to be practical (or impractical) to build should shape architecture decisions, not just follow from them.
Work with architects to turn spec behavior (e.g. entropy / load-balancing schemes, state-machine-driven congestion handling) into concrete, testable requirements, and help document and close gaps between specs, models, and RTL as they surface.
Support the software (SW), design verification (DV), and emulation teams by programming and tuning NPL parameters — and other chip-level parameters affected by NPL — throughout pre-silicon verification and emulation.
Play a central role in silicon bringup and hardware debug: bring the datapath up on real hardware, root-cause issues seen in the lab, and drive them to resolution across the NPL, architecture, and hardware boundaries. This is a significant and highly visible part of the job.
What we are Looking For
BS or MS in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
Experience spanning both networking / packet processing and chip-level design or verification (ASIC/SoC, DV). This combination of disciplines is fundamental to the role rather than incidental to it.
Solid fundamentals in digital logic and computer architecture, and fluency in at least one of C, C++, or Python.
Comfortable reading and reasoning about state machines, bit-level data structures, and dense specification documents.
Strong debugging instincts: comfortable digging into unexpected behavior, forming a hypothesis, and verifying it against real data rather than guessing.
Willingness to learn how NPL's logical constructs — tables, registers, functions, and dedicated hardware-accelerated blocks — get compiled and mapped onto the chip's flexible, programmable pipeline (shared bus resources, execution engines, and memory hierarchy). This compiler-driven mapping model is central to writing effective NPL and to reasoning about its behavior in verification and bringup.
Good verbal and written communication skills. Writing clear summaries and documentation — of models, findings, and spec/RTL gaps — is required, everyday work in this role, not an occasional task.
Nice to Have
﻿Hands-on experience with P4, NPL, or another domain-specific dataplane programming language — this matters more to us than general RTL / HDL experience.
Protocol-level experience (congestion control, ECN, load balancing, TCP) and the ability to debug distributed state machines and systems.
Experience with RDMA/RoCE is a significant plus.
Familiarity with AI/ML workloads — basic understanding of training and inference is welcome, and knowledge of collective communication operations is a significant plus.
Experience with RTL/C-model cross-validation or golden-model-based verification flows.
Scripting for test automation (Python) and comfort in a Linux environment.

title: Embedded Software Engineer
reason: Stack +28; Title fit +12; Exp fit +6; US +10
description_preview:
Join Us, and Ship Robots
Weave was founded to build the robots we’d want to have in our own home. We believe the next generation of robotics will transform everyday life by enabling people to do more and to reclaim time to spend on what’s important.
We also believe robots are in a sense like any other product: to matter, they have to ship. Our robots are already operating in real homes and businesses, giving us the opportunity to rapidly improve from real-world experience. With a growing team, strong customer demand, and capital for expansion, we’re entering an exciting stage of growth—and we’re looking for people with exceptional talent and standards to help bring home robotics to millions of households.
The Role
As an Embedded Software Engineer, you'll build the software closest to our hardware, on a compute platform we design ourselves: custom carrier boards, MCUs, and the sensors and actuators around them. MCU firmware, bus protocols, drivers, board bring-up, user-space drivers. When a new board arrives, you're the first person to make it do anything. You'll sit at the seam between electrical engineering and the rest of software, turning new hardware into a reliable platform the rest of the robotics stack can be built on.
Responsibilities
Develop production embedded software: Design, implement, test, and maintain embedded software for robotic systems using modern C++. Develop firmware, device drivers, communication stacks (SPI, I2C, RS-485, CAN/CAN FD, Ethernet, or EtherCAT), and interfaces for sensors, actuators, and other embedded peripherals.
Bring up new hardware: Collaborate with hardware and electrical engineers to integrate new circuits, and validate system functionality. You’ll need to be able to read and understand component datasheets to build and debug drivers for them.
Build real-time systems: Develop deterministic software that meets timing constraints while managing concurrency, resource limitations, and hardware failures.
Own the buses: GMSL SerDes links, RS-485, CAN, SPI/I²C. Electrical-to-software debugging with a scope and analyzer when a bug refuses to pick a layer. On the actuator bus you own the compute side; your peer Actuator Firmware engineer owns the other end.
Systematize bring-up: First power-on of new boards with the EE team, bring-up checklists that become manufacturing tests, and closing the gap between "works on my bench" and working on mass-produced units.
What You'll Bring
3+ years of experience developing embedded software: bare-metal, RTOS, and/or Linux-based platforms, ideally for robotics or other complex electromechanical systems.
Driver development experience: Extensive experience taking a new sensor, actuator, or peripheral from datasheet to a robust software interface, including initialization, configuration, error handling, diagnostics, and recovery.
Hardware-level debugging skill: Experience bringing up custom electronics and root-causing issues across hardware, firmware, and drivers using schematics, datasheets, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, debuggers, and protocol traces.
Experience building true real-time systems: you have a deep understanding of techniques to ensure real-time responsiveness and throughput in adversarial scenarios.
C and modern C++ fluency, with enough Python for tooling.
Nice to Have
Bootloader and secure-boot experience.
Production test tooling you built for a factory floor.
Time-sensitive sensors: hardware triggering, timestamping, or clock synchronization (PTP) for cameras, IMUs, or encoders.
Experience with Rust.

1,500 professionals

Application Developer
to join our IT organization. In this role, you will architect, build, optimize, and maintain high-performance Python applications deployed entirely across Google Cloud Platform (GCP).

Application Development & Architecture
Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain resilient Python applications utilizing Cloud Run, GKE, Cloud Functions, and Compute Engine.

description_preview:
Description
Want to work on next generation software services that build AWS Network? And design, build and own services that form the foundation of Network Configurations and Validations? If we've piqued your interest, read on, to learn more about this opportunity.
What do we do here? Amazon Web Services (AWS) runs one of the largest networks in the world. We are changing the way Networks are conceived, designed, built and operated, by adopting the principles of Software Defined Networking (SDN) and Intent Based Networking (IBN). We derive our network topologies from higher level designs and intents, and a distributed software system controls the way we manage our network. We put services and algorithms in place to control and manage all layers of the Amazon network, from top of the rack switches in our datacenters (TORs) to our internet and private backbone facing routers. In this software dev engineer position, you will be designing, building and owning highly distributed, large scale web services that form a core part of our SDN software ecosystem. You will work with a team of talented developers, and principal engineers to build the next generation software services in our space.
Why software services for building the network? At Amazon, we are always customer obsessed. By creating an intent-based, scalable network, we respond quickly and safely to network changes like scaling, maintenance, failure, security and other types of events. This also lowers the cost and overhead for customers, while driving up performance, availability and reliability.
Why now? We want to expand scope of our IBN and configuration backend systems to store and vend operational intent, there by facilitating anomaly detection. We also would expand our description languages, parsers and workflow engines to go beyond the mostly static configuration elements and cover dynamic and operational elements. To achieve this we need to expand our current team focusing on IBN related areas. We are looking for talented software engineers who want to get hands on experience with fully automated hyper scale data center networks, cloud infrastructure, large-scale software deployments, algorithms, distributed systems, lambda-based and service oriented architectures.
How do we operate in our team? We empower our engineers to take ownership of their realm and make a difference. They start by gathering requirements, diving deep to choose technologies, designing features and spinning new services, coding and reviewing, deploying software across the globe and maintaining services. In AWS, we are nimble and agile, like being part of a startup, innovating while collaborating with a smart group of people around you. We are thrilled about how software is changing the landscape of networking. We operate on an unimaginable scale. We push the boundaries in robustness, fault-tolerance and smart adaptive algorithms that can react intelligently to real-world events. Software engineers on our team contribute to every phase of the development process and deploy scalable software systems worldwide.
What will you be doing here?
Design and develop software services for network configuration, verification and management.
Work with your dev team build production quality software that meets our definition of done
Participate in sprint demos, reviews and planning sessions
Work alongside Senior Engineers and Principals to invent and simplify
Work with management, customers and other engineering teams to develop state of the art solutions, incorporating new technologies, algorithms and innovations.
Who are we looking for? Smart, talented engineers with solid, production quality, software services/applications experience. Previous Routing Protocols/Networking background is a plus. Have more questions? Talk to us! We'll be happy to setup an info call to give you more context and details about the job.
Basic Qualifications
3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
Experience programming with at least one software programming language
Preferred Qualifications
3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

description_preview:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.
Organization Overview
At Eli Lilly and Company, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. Lilly is a leader in global healthcare and has been discovering and developing medicines that help improve lives for more than 140 years. Our 50,000 employees around the world work as a team to bring breakthrough medicines to patients who need them. We are looking for motivated, highly skilled scientists and engineers to help us continue to bring breakthrough medicines to patients.
Delivery, Devices, and Connected Solutions (DDCS) sits within Lilly's Product Research & Development organization. We are a diverse team of scientists and engineers responsible for discovering, designing, and developing patient-centric drug delivery solutions across a broad range of modalities — from injection devices to novel routes of administration and nanomedicines. DDCS drives the drug delivery innovation agenda across early and late development to meet the needs of an expanding portfolio that spans small molecules, biologics, and nucleic acid therapeutics.
DDCS is organized around a matrix model with strong disciplinary and functional horizontals supporting innovation and commercialization verticals. Our vision is to get our medicines to more patients faster by accelerating reach and scale, guided by three strategic pillars: Delivery Systems, Robust & Sustainable, and Patient Experience + Outcomes.
Computational Modeling & Simulation (M&S) is a disciplinary horizontal within DDCS that builds and applies predictive models spanning molecular to system scales. M&S outputs inform device architecture, formulation and delivery-system design, and development strategy — reducing empirical iteration, quantifying risk, and building mechanistic understanding of how our delivery systems perform in real use. The scope of the capability spans continuum-scale multiphysics (CFD and FEA), molecular and mesoscale simulation, and scientific machine learning, working closely with Formulation Sciences, Device Engineering, Analytical Sciences, Manufacturing, Quality, and Regulatory.
Position Overview
This role builds hybrid physics-and-data models — and the agentic software layer that puts them in the hands of working scientists. It has two connected halves. The first is scientific machine learning: physics-informed networks, operator learning, multi-fidelity surrogates, Bayesian calibration, and gray-box system identification that accelerate or extend physics-based simulation. The second is AI engineering: agentic workflows that plan, set up, execute, and post-process modeling and simulation tasks by calling real solvers and real data, so that a scientist can move from question to credible answer without hand-assembling every step.
The role sits within the Computational Modeling & Simulation team in DDCS and works across the programs that the team supports. This is not a standalone research role: the models and tools are built with and for the drug product, device, and process development functions across Product Research & Development that use them. You will independently design, implement, validate, and support the workflows you build, working closely with the DDCS AI Application Development and Data Sciences functions on architecture, platform choices, and compliance.
Key Responsibilities
Scientific Machine Learning Development
Independently design, train, and validate SciML models — physics-informed neural networks, operator-learning architectures (e.g., DeepONet, Fourier neural operators), and Gaussian-process or multifidelity surrogates — against high-fidelity simulation and experimental data.
Apply Bayesian calibration and uncertainty quantification to deliver predictions with a defensible confidence statement rather than a point estimate.
Apply gray-box identification and symbolic-regression methods to infer unknown parameters or missing mechanisms from sparse experimental data.
Agentic Modeling Workflow Engineering
Design and build LLM-based agentic workflows that plan, set up, execute, monitor, and post-process modeling tasks by calling real tools — solvers (e.g., Abaqus, COMSOL, Ansys, OpenFOAM, LAMMPS, GROMACS), meshing and geometry utilities, HPC schedulers, and internal data services.
Implement the tool interfaces, APIs, and retrieval layers that connect agents to DDCS model libraries, simulation archives, and structured data sources.
Define and enforce human-in-the-loop checkpoints at the points where a modeling decision requires expert judgment rather than automation.
Package workflows so that a scientist who is not a software developer can use them reliably and unaided.
Credibility, Traceability, and Guardrails
Ensure every agent-executed run emits a complete provenance record: inputs, geometry and discretization, solver and library versions, convergence evidence, random seeds, and the human approvals applied.
Design for deterministic replay — any result that informs a decision must be reproducible from its recorded provenance, within a documented tolerance.
Build evaluation harnesses — benchmark problems with known solutions, regression tests, and reliability metrics — that quantify how often a workflow produces the right answer.

description_preview:
Why Join GEICO?
At GEICO, we offer a rewarding career where your ambitions are met with endless possibilities.
Every day we honor our iconic brand by offering quality coverage to millions of customers and being there when they need us most. We thrive on relentless innovation to exceed our customers' expectations while making a real impact on local communities nationwide.
Founded in 1936, GEICO is a member of the Berkshire Hathaway family of companies and one of the largest auto insurers in the United States. When you join our company, we want you to feel valued, supported, and proud to work here. That's why we offer the GEICO Pledge: Great Company, Great Culture, Great Rewards, and Great Careers.
The Contact Center Data Analytics Engineer I plays a critical role in improving contact center performance by turning operational, customer, and system data into reliable insights, reporting, and automation opportunities. This role supports the analytics needs of contact center operations, interactive voice response (IVR), self-service, workforce management, product, and technology partners. The ideal candidate combines strong technical skills with practical business judgment and can use data to proactively identify issues, explain performance trends, and recommend actions that improve customer experience, operational efficiency, and business outcomes.
This is a hybrid position, requiring on-site presence 2-3 days a week at one of the following locations: Dallas, TX; Palo Alto, CA; Bethesda, MD; Buffalo, NY; San Diego, CA; Virginia Beach, VA; Fredericksburg, VA; Tampa, FL.
Key Responsibilities
Develop, test, deploy, and maintain data structures, enterprise reports, dashboards, data visualizations, analytical systems, and recurring performance reporting.
Analyze contact center, IVR, digital, customer, and operational data to identify trends, root causes, performance gaps, and opportunities for automation or process improvement.
Build and maintain reporting using Power BI, SQL, Amazon QuickSight, Amazon CloudWatch, and other approved analytics tools used by the team.
Monitor key operational metrics and proactively identify emerging issues, including changes in call volume, containment, transfer behavior, speed of answer, abandonment, handle time, call drivers, and customer experience indicators.
Partner with operations, workforce management, IVR, automation, product, technology, data architecture, and data governance teams to understand business problems, define requirements, and design practical data solutions.
Research and query structured and unstructured data sources to understand how systems work, validate data quality, and expand available reporting and insight capabilities.
Create clear documentation for code, reporting logic, metric definitions, source systems, data structures, and operational assumptions.
Serve as a data steward for assigned subject areas, helping ensure data is accurate, available, properly classified, and governed appropriately.
Communicate findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, translating complex data into practical business recommendations.
Required Qualifications
1+ years of experience in business analytics, data analytics, product analytics, operations analytics, or a related analytical role.
1+ years of experience querying complex data sets using SQL and performing data analysis.
1+ years of experience using analytical or programming languages such as Python, R, SAS, .NET, M, or DAX.
Experience developing reporting or data visualizations in Power BI, Amazon QuickSight, Tableau, or similar business intelligence tools.
Ability to work with large and complex data sets, validate results, and explain findings in a clear and business-focused way.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, follow established processes, learn technical concepts quickly, and work effectively in a cross-functional environment.
BA/BS degree or equivalent experience in computer science, statistics, analytics, operations research, economics, mathematics, business, or a related field.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting contact center, IVR, customer service, workforce management, digital servicing, insurance, or financial technology environments.
Experience using Amazon CloudWatch or similar monitoring tools to identify system, service, or operational anomalies.
Experience working in an Agile environment with product, engineering, or technology teams.
Working knowledge of data governance, metric definition, data quality validation, and documentation practices.
Interest in automation, self-service improvement, and translating analytics into measurable business value.
Annual Salary
$79,950.00 - $141,450.00
The above annual salary range is a general guideline. Multiple factors are taken into consideration to arrive at the final hourly rate/ annual salary to be offered to the selected candidate. Factors include, but are not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the role, the selected candidate’s work experience, education and training, the work location as well as market and business considerations.

title: Manufacturing Systems Support Engineer- Night Shift
reason: Stack +31; Title fit +6; Poor fit -16; Entry +15; Exp fit +10; US +10
description_preview:
About Slate
At Slate, we’re building safe, reliable vehicles that people can afford, personalize and love—and doing it here in the USA as part of our commitment to reindustrialization. The spirit of DIY and customization runs throughout every element of a Slate, because people should have control over how their trucks look, feel, and represent them.
This position is based at the Slate manufacturing facility in Warsaw, IN. Nightshift hours are 7:00pm-3:30am. EDT
About Slate
At Slate, we’re building safe, reliable vehicles that people can afford, personalize and love—and doing it here in the USA as part of our commitment to reindustrialization. The spirit of DIY and customization runs throughout every element of a Slate, because people should have control over how their trucks look, feel, and represent them.
Who we are looking for
We are looking for a Manufacturing Systems Support Engineer to be the first line of defense when something goes wrong with Slate’s manufacturing technology stack. This is an entry-level role for someone who is technically grounded, methodically under pressure, and comfortable working on the factory floor alongside operators and supervisors as well as with software engineers and IT. You will diagnose and resolve issues across MES, WMS, CMMS, and their integrations — reading logs, querying data, following a hypothesis, and escalating with precision when you reach the limits of your access. If you are energized by troubleshooting real problems in a fast-moving environment and want to build deep expertise in how manufacturing software systems work, this is where that career starts.
What you get to do
Serve as the first point of contact for manufacturing system issues — triage incoming requests from operators, supervisors, and quality engineers across MES, WMS, and CMMS.
Diagnose software issues by reading application logs, querying databases, and tracing data flows to isolate whether a problem is a user error, a configuration issue, a data integrity problem, or a software defect.
Follow established troubleshooting runbooks to resolve known issue patterns; document any gaps or improvements you discover so the knowledge base stays accurate and genuinely useful.
Escalate to the software engineering team when an issue requires a code fix — write precise escalation tickets that include what you observed, what you ruled out, and what data supports your conclusion.
Monitor system health dashboards and act on anomalies before they become production-stopping events; know what normal looks like so you can recognize when something isn’t.
Analyze incident data to identify recurring patterns and high-frequency issue types — surface these trends to the engineering team with supporting data to drive permanent fixes rather than repeated workarounds.
Manage user administration tasks including account setup, access provisioning, and permission changes across manufacturing system platforms.
Support software release activities — execute test scripts, validate deployments against expected behavior, and flag regressions before they reach the production floor.
Walk the floor when the problem requires it — some issues only make sense when you see them in context at the station where they are happening.
What you bring to the team
Technical Skills
0–3 years of experience in IT support, helpdesk, technical operations, or a related role; exposure to manufacturing or industrial systems is a bonus but not expected.
Able to read and interpret application logs to distinguish a user error from a misconfiguration from a software defect — the error message is the starting point, not the answer.
Basic SQL: able to write straightforward queries to look up records, verify data integrity, cross-reference tables, and support incident investigation without needing a developer to pull the data for you.
Working understanding of how web-based software systems operate — browsers, REST APIs, databases, and how requests flow between them — sufficient to trace where in a stack something went wrong.
Experience using an ITSM ticketing system such as ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, Zendesk, or similar to manage and document support work.
Comfortable working in both Windows and Linux environments at an operator and configuration level.
Familiarity with monitoring or observability dashboards such as Grafana, Zabbix or Datadog is a plus.
Basic scripting ability in Python, Bash, or similar — not required, but valued and a strong indicator of the curiosity this role rewards.
How You Work
Methodical troubleshooter: you form a hypothesis, test it, confirm or rule it out, and move to the next one. You do not randomly change things hoping the problem goes away.
Clear communicator under pressure: when a production line is down, you can tell a supervisor what you know, what you are doing, and what you do not know yet — all in plain language, without adding to the panic.
Owns the ticket to closure: you do not close an issue until you have confirmed it is resolved, not just until the user stopped responding. Verified resolution is the bar.
Curious about root causes: “It’s working now” is not an acceptable end state when you do not know why it failed. You document what you found even when you cannot yet explain it, because that note prevents the next incident.
Comfortable on the floor: manufacturing environments are active and sometimes loud. You are willing to walk out to a station and observe a problem firsthand when context would help you diagnose it faster.
Keeps learning: manufacturing systems are broad and deep. You do not need to know everything on day one, but you should want to understand something new every week.
Experience And Education
Associate or bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, or a related field — or equivalent hands-on experience that demonstrates the same capabilities.
Manufacturing or industrial environment experience is welcomed but not required for a candidate with strong fun

title: Robotics Software Engineer, Simulation
reason: Stack +20; Title fit +12; Exp fit +6; US +10
description_preview:
Join Us, and Ship Robots
Weave was founded to build the robots we’d want to have in our own home. We believe the next generation of robotics will transform everyday life by enabling people to do more and to reclaim time to spend on what’s important.
We also believe robots are in a sense like any other product: to matter, they have to ship. Our robots are already operating in real homes and businesses, giving us the opportunity to rapidly improve from real-world experience. With a growing team, strong customer demand, and capital for expansion, we’re entering an exciting stage of growth—and we’re looking for people with exceptional talent and standards to help bring home robotics to millions of households.
The Role
Simulation is essential at nearly every level of our stack: validating kinematics, iterating on controls research, stress testing new mechanisms, trying new manipulation strategies, and proving out the robustness of our planning and SLAM stack. How fast all of those loops run, and how honestly simulation predicts hardware, is decided by the software this role owns.
You'll build our simulation platform as a core product with customers across the company: the environments, the models, and the fidelity work that makes "it works in sim" mean something.
Responsibilities
Own the sim stack. Isaac Lab, MuJoCo, or equivalent: environments, assets, robot models, and the tooling around them, kept current with every hardware revision that ships.
Model what matters. Actuator models (torque limits, friction, thermal behavior) and contact parameters identified against dyno and robot data with the motor control and controls teams; you know which fidelity buys transfer and which buys nothing.
Make training fast. GPU-parallel environment throughput, profiling, and the determinism and seeding discipline that make experiments reproducible.
Serve sim-to-real. System-identification pipelines, domain randomization tooling, and honest side-by-side measurement of where simulation and hardware disagree.
Catch regressions before hardware does. Scenario and regression suites that run controllers and policies in sim on every change.
Keep assets true. The pipeline from CAD and robot description to sim-ready assets, so simulation tracks the robot we actually build.
What You'll Bring
3+ years building simulation or robotics software, with deep hands-on experience in at least one modern robotics simulator (Isaac Lab/Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, Drake, or similar).
Physics literacy: knowledge of contact solvers, fabrics solvers, integrators, and friction models, including the specific limits of each.
Strong Python and C++ and the engineering habits to make a research-facing platform reliable.
Performance skill: you've profiled and scaled GPU-parallel workloads and treat environment throughput as a feature.
Respect for the real robot. You've compared sim to hardware honestly and changed the sim.
Nice to Have
RL training experience: you've been the customer of a sim stack and remember what hurt.
Rendering or synthetic-data experience for perception training.
USD or asset-pipeline experience at scale.

The Emerald Cloud Laboratory (ECL) enables life scientists to move out of the lab, and to conduct research entirely from a computer. Every scientist at Emerald learns to code, working in the Wolfram Language, and the eclectic team comes together to tackle the singular challenges at the intersection of understanding experimental detail, architecting the logistics for a new model of industrial lab facility, integrating new instrumentation, and building the software system that captures it all.

Our robots run real-time control, GPU inference, SLAM, camera pipelines, teleoperation, and networking on a compute platform we design ourselves: custom carrier boards, MCUs, and the sensor architecture around them. As a Systems Software Engineer focused on the OS, you'll own the OS layer and the IPC layer that connects it all: the kernel and its real-time behavior, scheduling, memory management, user-space drivers, time synchronization, and the shared-memory transport that moves data between processes with minimal copies and bounded latency. You'll also own how the system operates unattended: boot, OTA updates with rollback, service supervision, crash capture, and health monitoring.
Your software is the layer every other team builds on, and it ships on every robot. When new hardware arrives, you'll bring it up alongside electrical, controls, and robotics engineers.

System architecture: Design and implement the core systems that every robotics application depends on, including on-device and remote networking, IPC, scheduling, synchronization, and resource management.
Understand and optimize system performance: Profile, optimize, and understand the tradeoffs between CPU utilization, latency, throughput, memory usage, and scheduling behavior across the robotics software stack.
Design for reliability: Build diagnostics, health monitoring, and fault-handling systems that improve robot robustness and serviceability.
Debug across the stack: Investigate issues spanning hardware, firmware, and robotics software.
What You'll Bring
Deep Linux internals: 3+ years working at the OS level. Schedulers, memory, filesystems, and the kernel/userspace boundary.
Modern C++: Strong proficiency developing production-quality C++ software for embedded or real-time systems.
Systems programming: Strong understanding of Linux systems programming, including threading, synchronization, memory management, IPC, scheduling, and performance optimization, along with experience with the embedded Linux stack, including U-Boot, device trees, kernel configuration, DMA, and Buildroot or Yocto.
Hardware/software debugging: Comfortable reading schematics, probing hardware with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, and debugging issues that span electrical, firmware, and software boundaries. Experience using tools like gdb, strace, ltrace and others to understand system behavior.

Experience with Embedded Linux platform work: U-Boot, device trees, kernel config, DMA and the like.

Culture at Scribd, Inc.
We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.
We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.
So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.
This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.
About Our Team
The Growth Platform team is the infrastructure squad for Growth at Scribd. We build the shared services and tooling that the other Growth teams build on, and we empower marketers, lifecycle teams, and partner channels by delivering MarTech solutions that drive efficiency, data-informed decisions, and scalable user acquisition across our brands: Scribd, Everand, Slideshare, and Fable.
Our work spans self-service tooling, experimentation infrastructure, acquisition tracking and attribution, and integrations that share customer and event data with third-party platforms. Because we're a platform team, a lot of what we build ships through other teams' products, so we care about reliability and scalability, and about making our systems easy for others to build on. The team values collaboration, pragmatic problem-solving, and a culture of technical excellence.
About The Role
We are seeking a determined Fullstack Software Engineer to join our Growth Platform team. In this role, you will design, build, and scale the shared systems that power Growth at Scribd, from self-service tooling and experimentation infrastructure to the data integrations behind our lifecycle marketing.
You will partner closely with marketers, data analysts, lifecycle teams, and the other Growth engineering teams to deliver high-quality solutions that enhance cross-channel marketing effectiveness, attribution accuracy, and customer engagement. You’ll participate in technical design, code reviews, and best practice implementation while identifying opportunities to improve systems and processes.
Key Areas Of Responsibility Include
Building intuitive, performant self-service tools that let marketers and other teams move without engineering help.
Building and maintaining integrations that share customer and event data with third-party platforms, including our lifecycle marketing tools.
Ensuring scalability, testability, and maintainability throughout the development process.
Collaborating across teams to drive impactful projects forward.
Staying proactive by proposing innovative solutions to technical challenges.
What We’re Looking For
A passionate engineer who takes pride in writing clean, maintainable, and scalable code.
Someone who thrives in both backend system design and frontend feature development.
A strong communicator and collaborator who enjoys working with marketers, data scientists, product managers, and engineers across the Growth Pillar to develop high-leverage, self-service tools and data activation workflows.
An engineer who stays current with industry trends and technologies.
A pragmatic problem-solver who balances technical rigor with business needs.
Required Qualifications
3+ years of professional software development experience.
Proficiency with TypeScript, JavaScript, and modern frameworks like React.
Familiarity with Ruby on Rails and its ecosystem.
Understanding of database systems (SQL and NoSQL) and architectural tradeoffs.
Experience designing and consuming APIs (REST, GraphQL a plus).
Understanding of experimentation, A/B testing, personalization systems, and the MarTech landscape.
Communicates clearly and frequently with cross-functional partners, influencing through technical depth and collaborative decision-making.
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
Nice to Have
Experience with instrumenting and working on data integration projects, such as event tracking, data pipelines, or syncing user data between internal systems and third-party platforms.
Have worked in a Growth Engineering or Growth Platform team at a product-led company.
Experience with backend technologies like Redis, Kafka, MySQL, and Terraform.
Knowledge of GraphQL and Next.js.
Familiarity with migrating monolithic architectures to microservices/frontends.

Responsibilities

The Global Traffic Architecture (GTA) team at ByteDance designs, builds, and operates large-scale, multi-cloud network services that accelerate and optimize traffic for TikTok and a broad portfolio of ByteDance applications. Our platform provides core capabilities including L4/L7 load balancing, L4/L7 traffic acceleration, global ingress, and forward proxy. Joining GTA means working with a world-class engineering team to build TikTok-scale network infrastructure that serves billions of users worldwide.
To support TikTok's continued global growth, the GTA team is hiring engineers to help build the next generation of our multi-cloud, cloud-native traffic architecture.
We are looking for talented individuals to join our team. As a graduate, you will get opportunities to pursue bold ideas, tackle complex challenges, and unlock limitless growth.
Successful candidates must be able to commit to an onboarding date by the end of the year. Please state your availability and graduation date clearly in your resume.

Design and develop core traffic software, including L4/L7 load balancers and caching systems, to process terabyte-scale data in real time.
Build data pipelines and telemetry systems that enable data-driven traffic control.
Develop API acceleration and other networking services on top of our multi-cloud traffic platform.
Troubleshoot production issues and improve the performance, reliability, and scalability of online traffic systems.
Research and apply emerging technologies to make traffic processing more efficient and scalable.
Build platform capabilities, including control planes, self-service APIs, developer tooling, and supporting infrastructure, for the Global Traffic Architecture.
Integrate Agent capabilities from ByteDance's internal platforms into engineering workflows to improve research and development efficiency across the traffic platform.

Individuals who are pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
Proficiency in one or more of Python, Go, Rust, C, or C++, with hands-on experience in Linux environments.
Solid understanding of core networking concepts and protocols, including TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, and DNS.
Familiarity with AI application development and the ability to integrate Agent capabilities from ByteDance's internal platforms into engineering workflows to improve research and development efficiency.
Strong problem-solving skills, a willingness to learn, and the ability to collaborate effectively in a fast-paced engineering environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with systems, networking, distributed systems, or cloud infrastructure through coursework, internships, research, projects, or open-source contributions.
Experience with proxy software such as Nginx or Envoy.
Familiarity with modern network protocols such as HTTP/2, HTTP/3 (QUIC), and TLS 1.3.

We are looking for a Controls Programmer who thrives on solving problems and making machines move.
Position Summary
If you enjoy turning electrical and mechanical concepts into reliable, working automation, this is a role where your contribution will be visible every day. We are seeking a Controls Programmer I to join our team and help program, debug, and commission custom machinery. You will work alongside experienced mechanical and electrical technicians to solve real-world problems, validate machine operation, and make sure each system is ready to perform.

Write and debug PLC code in accordance with work instructions, project specifications, and customer requirements.
Program graphic user interfaces that help operators interact confidently with automated equipment.

Maintain accurate project documentation, including drawings, parts lists, calibration data, wire lists, and specifications.
Support machine-manual development and occasional field service work for installation, modification, and system support.
Contribute ideas that improve processes, quality, and the way our team works.

Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related engineering discipline.
A working knowledge of ladder logic programming for a variety of PLC platforms.
Familiarity with PLC networks, communications, and hardware and software interfaces.
Knowledge of foundational electrical concepts, including PNP and NPN switches, AC and DC circuits, E-Stop circuits, and stepper or servo motor function.
The ability to read and understand electrical prints and technical documents.
A safety-first mindset and willingness to work in an active, hands-on environment, including occasional travel when needed.
If you are ready to grow your controls career, work closely with talented technicians, and see your code power real machines, we would love to hear from you. Apply now and help us build automation that performs.

We are building real-world Physical AI systems where models interact with physical machines. Day to day, you will design simulation environments, produce large volumes of labeled synthetic data, train and evaluate learned policies, and work with engineers across robotics, controls, and perception to close the sim-to-real gap. Build and maintain high-fidelity, physics-accurate simulation environments in NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim for training, testing, and validating robotic systems.

Design and run reinforcement learning and imitation learning pipelines using simulation-generated and synthetic data.

Drive simulation-to-real transfer through domain randomization, system identification, and validation on physical systems.

Integrate foundation models to support reasoning, task decomposition, and human-in-the-loop learning.

Hands-on experience training robotic agents in simulation, on physical systems, or both.
Strong background in reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or learning-based control, including domain randomization and curriculum learning.
Proven experience building simulation environments in NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac Sim, or Isaac Lab, or comparable GPU-accelerated simulation platforms.

Builder mindset with a track record of moving learning systems from experiment to deployment.
